claims.text: W-Ta-Cr-V refractory high-entropy alloys have demonstrated high thermal and irradiation resistance.
The baseline W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA has a single-phase microstructure.
W-based RHEAs are suitable for high-temperature applications and can exhibit superior high-temperature strength.
A controlled dispersion of nanoscale oxide nanoparticles such as Y2O3 can be introduced into a W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA by advanced powder synthesis or mechanical alloying.
The intervention will produce a uniform nanoscale oxide dispersion embedded in the RHEA matrix.
The oxide nanoparticles will remain stable during exposure above 1000°C and under high-dose irradiation.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles impede dislocation motion by acting as pinning sites.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles trap irradiation-induced defects.
Dislocation pinning by the nanoparticles will increase yield strength relative to the nanoparticle-free RHEA.
The nanoparticle dispersion will increase ductility relative to the nanoparticle-free RHEA.
The nanoparticle-dispersed alloy will retain a single-phase microstructure during prolonged high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
The nanoparticle-dispersed alloy will resist irradiation-induced defect accumulation.

The previously developed W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA exhibited no noticeable dislocation-loop formation, smaller helium bubbles, and no radiation-induced grain-boundary segregation under the reported irradiation and implantation conditions.
Excessive oxide content or nanoparticle agglomeration could embrittle the alloy.
Excessive oxide content or nanoparticle agglomeration could destabilize the alloy microstructure.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property improvement may vary with nanoparticle loading and alloy composition.
Prior evidence from oxide-dispersion-strengthened alloys supports the proposed strengthening mechanism.
